notes:
The home screen is a live cockpit now, not a page of buttons.

The last release had the theme, the type and the icons right and the structure wrong. It showed a large card that said "CarPlay", an empty box, four dashes and "Nothing playing" - every element was about content rather than being content, and a screen of nothing looks unfinished no matter how carefully it is set. The whole point of this app is live windows, and the redesign had quietly turned it into a launcher grid.

The top two thirds of the screen are panes. A pane is a slot rather than an app: it holds a list of sources and a swipe across its header moves between them - the reversing camera, the app drawer, a gauge, a web dashboard, a clock, or a real app running in its own resizable window. One pane, two side by side, or three, with a divider you can drag to change the split. Nothing forces two apps to be open at once, and the app drawer being available inside a pane means reaching any app never requires leaving the cockpit.

This works because the head unit really does allow third-party apps to open as floating resizable windows, which was confirmed on the device some time ago. Moving a window is done by relaunching it at new bounds, which reuses the existing task rather than opening a second copy, so dragging the divider moves the apps rather than restarting them.

One consequence is worth knowing, because it shaped the design. An app window floats above this launcher and receives all the touches inside itself, so a swipe starting over a map would be taken by the map. That is why every pane has a slim header strip along its top - it is the one part of a pane that always belongs to DWM, and it is where the swipe and the position dots live.

The bottom third is dense instrumentation instead of four half-empty cards. Eight readings on a single line: speed, gear, coolant, battery, fuel, engine, boost and outside temperature. A schematic of the vehicle from above carrying door and tailgate state, tyre pressures at their corners, the parking sensor ring and the steering-predicted guide lines when reversing. A music strip with real album artwork and a progress bar, which had been thrown away for a placeholder. And six large shortcuts.

Transmission temperature is deliberately not there. It is not a standard diagnostic reading and this vehicle does not send it, and a slot that can never fill is worse than no slot at all.

The accent colour is now ice blue rather than the blue Android ships with. It reads closer to a modern factory system, and it holds its own against a bright map or a daylight camera picture sitting next to it.

Four faults were found by rendering the screen and looking at it rather than by reasoning about the code. The vehicle drawing came out wider than it was long because its proportions assumed a tall space. The album art expanded to fill the row and squeezed the song title down to nothing, so the track name vanished entirely. The gear letters were about to be printed backwards, because this vehicle numbers Park and Drive the opposite way round to the obvious guess. And the shortcuts drifted apart across their box when there were only three of them.

Web panels now have a lifecycle for the first time. Exactly one runs at a time and the rest are held paused, keeping their last picture. Until now a web panel kept its timers, its scripts and any video running even while the launcher was in the background, on a device with very little memory to spare.

Six views of the cockpit are rendered at the real panel size and stored in the repository, so any future change that disturbs them fails the build.

Two things still need checking in the truck: whether a window can be parked off-screen when you swipe a pane away from an app, and whether the divider can be grabbed in the gap between two windows.
